## Observation
On origin/main 38f8587f65d (2026-10-30), running these together with -n 4 fails 22 tests in tests/unit/reconciler/orchestrate/test_reconcile_once.py:

pytest -q -n 4 tests/unit/reconciler/state tests/unit/reconciler/test_lock_steal.py tests/unit/reconciler/test_lock_orphan_local_ref.py tests/unit/test_last_pass_backoff_jitter_paediatric.py tests/unit/test_raw_git_write_lint.py tests/scripts/graph/test_repair_pause_ownership.py tests/interfaces/store tests/interfaces/facades tests/scripts/test_canary_status_refs_heldout.py tests/unit/reconciler/orchestrate

15 fail with BackendEnvError 'empty Jira Cloud read scope: the configured project (jira.project / JIRA_PROJECT) is unset' and 7 with ValueError 'inbound fetch requires a valid jira.project key ... got '''. The same tests pass when tests/unit/reconciler/orchestrate runs with only tests/unit/reconciler/state and tests/interfaces/store + facades in a different grouping, and CI's gating cell is green, so the outcome depends on which tests share a worker. Reproduced twice on the same host (once with the S3 lock change applied, once on unmodified main).

## Hypotheses
A test in the co-scheduled set mutates process-wide Jira config (JIRA_PROJECT env, a cached rebar config, or a module-level project setting) without restoring it; or test_reconcile_once depends on config another test happens to set first. Unproven.

## Plan
1. Bisect the co-scheduled files with -p no:randomly -n 0 to find the first test after which test_reconcile_once fails.
2. Identify the leaked state and fix the leak at its source (or make test_reconcile_once set its own project explicitly if it is relying on leaked state).
3. Add a regression check that runs the polluting test before test_reconcile_once.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The command above passes on main.
- [ ] The polluting test and the leaked state are named on this ticket.
- [ ] A regression test fails before the fix and passes after.
